images.title: Choosing a scale of 10
images.purpose: Show that with 1 unit = 10 runs, a score is shown by dividing by 10, so 100 runs becomes a bar 10 units tall.
images.composition: A vertical scale line at left with two tall bars beside it, wide space around, and one scale note at the top right.
images.exact_structure: One vertical grey #6B7280 scale line with exactly 11 equal-spaced ticks from 0 to 10 units. Two bars of equal width standing on a baseline: teal #0072B2 bar exactly 10 units tall, amber #E69F00 bar exactly 5 units tall (half the teal bar). Only ticks 0, 5 and 10 carry numbers. Exactly 2 bars and 1 scale line.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
bar heights not in the ratio 2 to 1, or uneven tick spacing
images.takeaway: With 1 unit = 10 runs, divide each score by 10 to get the bar height.
images.description: A scale from 0 to 10 units with a teal bar 10 units tall for 100 runs and an amber bar 5 units tall for 50 runs.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say how many runs one unit stands for, then read off the height of each bar.

image_decisions.why: The key idea is the scale choice; two bars show the divide-by-10 rule without crowding.
